text:
tara: After applying the NS + RBAC tighten in priv-db, I noticed outbound TLS to 23.45.67.89 from svcaccount:db-secrets-writer. Not in our allowlist. Anyone oncall?

ops-bot: [ALERT] priv-db egress anomaly 2026-07-12T02:15Z detected 19 connections to 23.45.67.89 from system:serviceaccount:priv-db:db-secrets-writer.

anita: Oncall. Can you paste the exact kubectl patch you applied and the pod names? Run `kubectl get rolebinding -n priv-db -o yaml | grep -C3 db-secrets-writer` and collect kube-audit lines.

tara: Patch was `kubectl patch rolebinding priv-db-secrets -n priv-db --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/roleRef/name","value":"secrets-reader"}]'` at 02:13:42Z. Pods: db-secrets-writer-0.

dinesh: VPC flow logs show NAT-gw-2 used at 02:14:01. Suggest immediate containment: rotate SA token, patch pod to temp-noegress SA, and add VPC deny for 23.45.67.89. Also snapshot pod fs for forensics.

kevin: I'll patch to temp-noegress and restart the pod now. Command: `kubectl create sa temp-noegress -n priv-db && kubectl patch deploy db-secrets -n priv-db -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"serviceAccountName":"temp-noegress"}}}}' && kubectl rollout restart deploy/db-secrets -n priv-db`.

maria: I'll open vuln-triage INC-2026-782 and collect kube-apiserver audit, node journal, and our egress-proxy traces. If the KMS host resolves external, legal needs to be looped in.

anita: Quick check: grep audit for "user":{"username":"system:serviceaccount:priv-db:db-secrets-writer"} and `decrypt` verb. If we see repeated decrypts right after the RBAC change it's likely cached retries. After containment, add an egress smoke test to the RBAC change runbook.

tara: Containment done. Pod restarted with temp SA and egress deny applied. Monitoring for repeats. I'll upload artifacts to the ticket.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-782 created. Assignees: anita, dinesh, kevin. Priority: P2.

anita: Postmortem actions: 1) require an egress smoke test post-RBAC changes touching secrets 2) enforce short TTLs for SA tokens and auto-rotation 3) add alerting for KMS-host hits from private clusters 4) scan images for baked-in creds.

tara: Thanks all, will follow up with timeline and evidence in the ticket.
